to fill someone with the urge to act

questions.q: Explain the effect of anaphora in 'we shall fight...' repeated.
questions.a: It builds rhythm and determination; the repeated 'we' unites the nation.

questions.q: Name one method Antony shares with these speeches.
questions.a: Repetition ('honourable man'), rhetorical questions, or direct address ('Friends, Romans, countrymen').

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, compare one real speech with Antony's: one shared method and one difference in purpose. Starter: 'Both speakers use...'
questions.a: A comparison: shared method (repetition or direct address) and difference (inspiring courage versus stirring revenge).

questions.q: Extend: how does the context of each speech add to its power?
questions.a: Fear of invasion; grief and confusion after Caesar's death.

questions.q: Stretch: should a speaker be judged by methods or by purpose?
questions.a: By purpose: the same methods can inspire courage or incite violence.

questions.q: Repeating 'we shall fight' at the start of lines is...
questions.a: C) anaphora. Anaphora repeats openings; the others are different methods.

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: A speech is remembered when powerful methods meet a moment of real crisis.
